messages.readiness.ready: Ready. Enable explicitly when you want to start capture.
messages.readiness.incomplete: The host has not reported readiness. Check again; if this persists, inspect the host logs.
messages.readiness.cannotEnable: Resolve the blocking conditions above, then check again.
messages.readiness.privileges: Grant network administration permission on the KONE host, then restart KONE with the same profile. Linux requires CAP_NET_ADMIN; Windows/macOS require administrator authorization. The browser cannot grant OS permissions.
messages.readiness.inbound_disabled: Enable the TUN inbound in capture settings, save, then check again.
messages.readiness.inbound: TUN is configured and enabled. It only starts capturing after you explicitly enable it.
messages.readiness.dns_source: Discover original system DNS at startup; Host/Gate use public defaults with a warning only when no usable default upstream is found.
messages.readiness.capture_scope: Only Fake-IP and explicit CIDR routes enter KONE. Other direct traffic may remain outside capture.
messages.readiness.configuration: Repair the saved configuration before enabling. The technical details identify the invalid field or reference.
messages.readiness.direct_only: No proxy rules are configured. Unmatched traffic uses built-in direct routing; no proxy setup or additional confirmation is needed.
messages.readiness.outbound_disabled: Enable the outbound selected by your rules, or choose another one. Connections using the disabled outbound will be rejected.
messages.readiness.outbound_warning: This outbound has no current successful test. You can test it explicitly or continue without testing.
messages.readiness.outbound_error: The latest test failed. Review the outbound or continue explicitly; startup is allowed, but affected connections may fail.
messages.readiness.outbound_ready: The outbound passed a recent explicit TCP test.
messages.readiness.dns_scope: Domain interception depends on clients using KONE DNS. Encrypted DNS may bypass it; traffic without IPv6 capture may also bypass KONE.
messages.readiness.ipv6_platform: Review IPv6 capture settings and platform support before enabling.
messages.readiness.device_exists: Choose an unused TUN name. If a previous KONE run left resources behind, inspect recovery before changing them.
messages.readiness.outbound_interface: Select an available physical outbound interface in capture settings.
messages.readiness.interfaces: The host could not read interface addresses. Inspect the technical error and host permissions, then check again.
messages.readiness.network_overlap: Choose a TUN IPv4 subnet that does not overlap existing LAN or VPN interfaces.
messages.readiness.ipv6_network_overlap: Choose a TUN IPv6 subnet that does not overlap existing interfaces.
messages.readiness.canceled: The check did not finish. Check again before enabling.
messages.readiness.preflight: Review the host environment and technical details, then check again.

messages.access.allHint: Includes public IPv4 interfaces, if present.

messages.access.passwordLogin: Sign in with the management password.

messages.access.caMac: macOS: import the CA in Keychain Access, open its Trust settings, and trust it for SSL.
messages.access.caBrowser: Other devices: import the CA in the system or browser certificate settings, then enable trust for websites.
messages.access.copyFailed: Copy failed. Select and copy the value manually.

messages.api.access_bind: Could not bind this address and port. Check whether the port is in use.
messages.api.access_restore: The listener change failed and the previous listener could not be restored. Choose an available port and enable it again.
messages.api.access_password: Set a management password before enabling remote access.

messages.policy.protection.proxyHint: KONE connects to these endpoints outside capture. Other services on the same host follow routing rules.
messages.policy.protection.dnsHint: KONE’s upstream queries bypass capture; this does not force all traffic to these IPs to go direct.
messages.policy.protection.autoDNS: Automatic upstreams are selected from the host’s DNS context at startup.
messages.outbounds.autoSummary: Automatic checks every 60 seconds, one at a time. Targets and TLS are configurable per outbound.
messages.outbounds.autoHelp: Runs while KONE is open, even with capture paused. Uses the configured proxy protocol and target; it does not inspect user traffic or prove UDP availability.
messages.outbounds.disableHint: Disabling makes connections routed to this outbound fail; it does not fall back to direct.
messages.outbounds.authRemoved: Authentication will be removed on save
messages.diagnostics.title: Network diagnostics
messages.readiness.authorization: Click Enable proxy, then approve the system authorization dialog on the KONE host. No restart is required. A remote browser cannot display this dialog.
messages.readiness.authorization_unavailable: Install pkexec and a polkit authentication agent on the Linux host, then check again. On a headless host, start KONE with network administration privileges and the same profile directory.
messages.api.authorization_unavailable: System authorization is unavailable. Install pkexec and a polkit authentication agent on the KONE host, or run with network administration privileges.
messages.api.authorization_failed: System authorization failed. Check that a polkit authentication agent is running in the KONE host’s desktop session, then retry. Headless hosts need network administration privileges at launch.
messages.api.authorization_canceled: Authorization was canceled. The proxy remains paused; click Enable proxy to retry.
messages.api.authorization_pending: Finish or cancel the previous system authorization dialog on the KONE host before retrying.
messages.diagnostics.historyEmpty: Type a target to run a new test.
messages.diagnostics.dnsHint: Query the same domain through system DNS and KONE DNS. No server address or outbound is needed.
messages.diagnostics.elapsedHint: Total time includes name resolution, connection, proxy negotiation and target TLS when enabled. No HTTP page is requested. Endpoint TCP time only measures the first connection to the destination or proxy.
messages.diagnostics.dnsElapsedHint: Total time runs from the start of this test through validation of the UDP DNS response; it includes resolution and proxy negotiation.
messages.proxy.awaitingAuthorization: Enabling · approve any system dialog on the KONE host
messages.diagnostics.dnsEmpty: Compare the domain using both DNS paths.
messages.api.helper_start_failed: The network helper could not start or connect. Check the KONE executable and local IPC access, then retry; the proxy remains paused.
messages.readiness.system_dns: Host DNS integration could not complete. Check host authorization, the resolver configuration and port 53 in the technical details.
messages.diagnostics.defaultPort: No port specified? TCP uses port 80. Enable TLS only when the target supports it.
messages.diagnostics.dnsPathsHint: System DNS uses the host’s current resolver, which may already point to KONE. KONE DNS includes its cache, rules and Fake-IP; while paused, it uses saved settings without enabling capture.
messages.diagnostics.virtualAnswers: Contains KONE Fake-IP addresses. These represent proxy rules, not the server’s public address.
messages.resolvers.hostHint: KONE takes over this PC’s system DNS while capture is enabled, then restores the original settings when paused.
messages.resolvers.gateHint: Serve DNS for LAN clients without changing this host’s system DNS.
messages.resolvers.hostPath: System DNS → KONE → original system upstreams
messages.resolvers.gateSetup: Set this LAN address as DNS in your router’s DHCP settings or on clients. Standard DNS uses port 53. Route KONE’s Fake-IP network back to this host for proxy domain rules.
messages.resolvers.automaticHint: Both modes discover the current system DNS before capture starts and keep that snapshot as their upstreams.
messages.resolvers.runningUpstreamHint: Showing the running engine’s upstreams. Automatic settings are discovered again before the next start.
messages.resolvers.publicFallback: No usable system DNS was discovered. Public defaults are in use: Google (8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4) and Cloudflare (1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1). Their reachability has not been tested; you can set custom upstreams.
messages.resolvers.customHint: One IP per line; append :port for a nonstandard port. Explicit upstream failures do not silently switch to public DNS.
messages.resolvers.pausedHint: DNS listeners and system DNS changes start only when you enable capture. Saving does not start them.
messages.resolvers.advanced: Advanced · domain routes, cache and timeouts
messages.resolvers.saveHint: Pause capture before applying DNS changes. Choose a mode, then configure its upstreams.
messages.resolvers.legacyHint: This saved configuration does not manage system DNS. Choose Host or Gate explicitly to migrate; KONE will not open a LAN listener automatically.
messages.errors.system_dns: Host DNS integration could not complete. Check host authorization, the resolver configuration and port 53 in the technical details.
messages.errors.dns_listener: DNS could not listen on the configured address. Check that the interface exists and the port is free.
messages.api.system_dns: Host DNS integration could not complete. Check host authorization, the resolver configuration and port 53 in the technical details.
messages.api.dns_listener: DNS could not listen on the configured address. Check that the interface exists and the port is free.
messages.readiness.dns_listener: DNS could not listen on the configured address. Check that the interface exists and the port is free.
messages.policy.layeredOrder: System protection → Domain rules → IP rules → Default
messages.policy.legacyOrder: Legacy order · rules still follow the saved file order
messages.policy.upgradeToggle: Use layered rules and durable Fake-IP ownership
messages.policy.upgradeHint: Preview precedence changes and a new address pool. Capture must be paused. Existing rules keep their order within each group.
messages.policy.upgradePreview: Original domain rules precede aliases and IP rules. Old virtual addresses remain captured and rejected; applications must resolve again.
messages.policy.pool.domainHint: Original name first; then related aliases. First match within this group.
messages.policy.pool.ipHint: Checked after domain rules, using verified address candidates.
messages.policy.evidence.complete: Decision based on the available target evidence.
messages.policy.evidence.dns_required: DNS evidence is required. This simulation does not resolve the target or assume a default result.
messages.policy.evidence.flow_required: The application protocol or port is required before selecting an outbound.
messages.policy.evidence.dns_failed: Required DNS evidence is unavailable; no fallback decision was made.
messages.resolvers.ownershipHint: Ownership survives cache expiry and restart. Published addresses are never reassigned to another domain.
messages.resolvers.volatileHint: Legacy in-memory ownership. Preview an upgrade from Proxy rules before switching address pools.
messages.resolvers.poolCapacity: Pool nearly full; existing ownership is retained when new allocations stop.
messages.errors.fake_ip_ownership: Fake-IP ownership could not be restored or committed. Preserve the state files and inspect the technical details before restarting.
messages.api.fake_ip_ownership: Fake-IP ownership could not be restored or committed. Preserve the state files and inspect the technical details before restarting.
messages.smart.title: Smart suggestions
messages.smart.consent: Opt-in background TCP/443 and TLS probes of public targets observed in business DNS. Suggestions only; no automatic routing changes.
messages.smart.upgrade: Upgrade to layered rules before enabling Smart. Existing rules keep their saved order until you confirm the upgrade.
messages.smart.sharedProxy: Shared with the default proxy policy. Change this outbound in the base policy editor.
messages.smart.empty: Waiting for new business DNS queries. Explicit rules, private targets and short-lived evidence are excluded.
messages.smart.pausedHint: Capture is paused. Enable it to observe new DNS queries; opening this page does not start probes.
messages.smart.scope: KONE probe, not application traffic. Port 443 is a Web default, not an observed application port. TLS verification covers only the tested endpoint; no HTTP request is sent.
messages.smart.partial: Some DNS candidates were not tested within the budget. Results cover sampled addresses only.
messages.smart.ruleLifetime: Exact domain, TCP/443 only. This rule stays enabled until you edit or remove it, including when Smart is off.
messages.smart.cacheBoundary: Newly resolved connections use the rule. Existing connections keep their path; cached real IPs may need a fresh DNS lookup. No shared IP route is added.
messages.smart.accepted: Rule saved. Re-resolve the domain and start a new connection to verify it.
messages.api.smart_stale: This suggestion is no longer current. Wait for a new DNS query or recheck the evidence.
messages.resolvers.ledgerSize: Ownership storage: {{used}} / {{limit}} MiB. Clearing DNS cache does not release address identities.
messages.smart.preferredInUse: Choose another preferred proxy in Proxy rules before disabling or deleting this outbound.
messages.smart.proxyNotCompared: The proxy was not compared. Direct TLS success does not establish a speed advantage or the correct exit location for your application.
